title: Existence of a free variable when no term is fixed and not all are killed
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables and let $\rho$ be a restriction on those variables. Suppose that not every term of $f$ is killed by $\rho$, and that no term of $f$ is fixed by $\rho$. Then $\rho$ leaves at least one variable free; that is, there exists an index $v \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\rho(v)$ unset.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
ρ is a restriction on n variables
not every term of f is killed by ρ
no term of f is fixed by ρ
replaced:
For a DNF $f$ and restriction $\rho$, if not every term is killed by $\rho$ and no term
is fixed by $\rho$, then $\rho$ has at least one free variable $v \in \rho.\mathrm{freeVars}$.
